title: Check if all list items share a type
description: Write a function `same_data_type(items)` that returns whether every item in `items` has the same type.
hints: Idea to consider: collect every item's type into a set
{type(item) for item in items} is a set comprehension - it collapses every item's type down to the distinct ones present. If only one type appears, the set has exactly one element.
Build a set of type(item) for item in items, and return whether its length is 1 (or 0, for an empty list - already 'the same type' by default).
expected_behavior: Returns True if every item has the same type (or the list is empty).
solution:
def same_data_type(items):
    return len({type(item) for item in items}) <= 1
explanation: A set comprehension over the types (not the values) answers 'how many distinct types are present' in one expression - at most 1 means uniform, same idea as all_unique but applied to types instead of values.
